lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 10: probes and graceful shutdown
lesson.description: Add liveness, readiness and startup probes, watch each one fail on purpose, and shut Pods down cleanly with preStop hooks and SIGTERM.
lesson.tested: Ran every probe and shutdown example on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Readiness decides who gets traffic, liveness decides who gets restarted, and every container must exit cleanly on SIGTERM inside its grace period.

cheatsheet.intro: The three probes, shutdown, and the commands from Lesson 10.

boards.title: Three probes
boards.hint: what each one is allowed to do

rows.name: startupProbe
rows.role: Covers start time. Allows `failureThreshold` times `periodSeconds` to start.
rows.where: keeps liveness from killing a slow start

rows.name: livenessProbe
rows.role: Restarts a stuck container after `failureThreshold` failures in a row.
rows.where: keep it about the process itself

rows.name: readinessProbe
rows.role: Decides whether the Pod gets Service traffic. No restart.

rows.name: tcpSocket
rows.role: Passes if the port accepts a connection.

steps.title: How a Pod is stopped
steps.hint: the clock starts before the hook

items.what: `lifecycle.preStop` can be `sleep`, `exec` or `httpGet`. It runs before SIGTERM.
Then the kubelet sends SIGTERM. A process that ignores it waits out the grace period.
When `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` ends, the container is killed. The default is 30 seconds and covers the hook plus the app's own shutdown.
`lastState` exit 137 means SIGKILL. The hook and the shutdown share one budget.

commands.note: skips the wait; use with care

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster and the namespace `k8s-from-zero` from part 4. The lesson's cluster is `k8s-ep10`. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does each of the three probes decide?
exercises.a: Startup covers start time. Liveness restarts a stuck container. Readiness decides whether a Pod gets Service traffic.

exercises.q: Does a failing readiness probe restart the Pod?
exercises.a: No. It sets the endpoint's `ready` condition to false. The Pod keeps running.

exercises.q: In what order does a delete run, and when does the clock start?
exercises.a: The preStop hook, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL when the grace period ends. The clock starts before the hook. The default grace period is 30 seconds.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: These are the failures the lesson caused.

exercises.q: A readiness probe points at port 8080, where nginx does not listen. What does rollout status print, and which Pods keep serving?
exercises.a: `error: timed out waiting for the condition`. The new Pod sits at `0/1` with `Readiness probe failed` and connection refused. The old Pods keep serving. Fix the manifest and apply it, or `kubectl rollout undo`.

exercises.q: RESTARTS climbs and events say `failed liveness probe, will be restarted`. What two causes does the lesson name, and where do dependency checks belong?
exercises.a: The probe may be too strict, such as a 1-second `timeoutSeconds` on a slow endpoint, or the app may need longer to start. Use a startup probe for start time. Keep liveness about the process itself. Put dependency checks in readiness, if anywhere.

exercises.q: Every delete takes 30 seconds. What is the process doing, and what does the lesson say about wrapper scripts?
exercises.a: The process ignores SIGTERM. Common causes: a shell script as process 1 without `trap`, or a shell wrapper that starts the real app as a child so the signal never reaches it. Use `exec` in wrapper scripts, or handle the signal.

exercises.q: A preStop hook needs 55 seconds and the app needs 10, with a 60-second grace period. What happens?
exercises.a: The hook and the shutdown share one budget. A 60-second grace period kills the app mid-shutdown. Raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to cover both.
